gascoigne is a token optimizer for LLM agents. It sits between an agent and what the agent
reads (shell output, MCP tool results, web pages), shrinks it, and keeps every original in a
local ledger so nothing is ever lost.

Output gascoigne already optimized (exec, its MCP server, the proxy) is recognized by its
hint and left alone, as are gascoigne's own MCP tools. **Read** is never replaced: Claude
numbers the lines it shows, and dropped lines would shift those numbers. **WebSearch** is
left too: its results (a median of 608 tokens in measured sessions) are rendered by Claude
Code from a fixed structure.

Measured on 16 Claude Code sessions (3,148 tool results): a tool result stays in context for
a **median 110 later requests** (mean 145, deciles 17–335), and 0.8% of gaps between
requests exceed the 5-minute cache TTL. So rereads, not the first read, make up most of the
cost: on Opus 5.5 a token saved is worth $5/MTok at first read and about $31/MTok in
context.

Most new support is a **dialect**: a new tool in a family gascoigne already has. A new
**optimizer** is only for a new family. Other component kinds (receivers, filters,
exporters, extensions) follow the same package shape.

Every run appears as it happens, with its savings, content type and, when it was not
optimized, the reason. Click a run to compare the original with what the agent read, side by
side, and see each optimizer's step.

Ids are the first 8 hex digits of the text's sha256 (12, 16 or 64 when that prefix holds a
different text), so the same output from any session is stored once and its hint costs ~7
fewer tokens. Originals are gzip-compressed. Source keys longer than 200 bytes (whole
command lines, heredocs) are stored as a 160-byte prefix plus a hash. Ledgers from older
versions are converted on first open and vacuumed (a real one: 22 MB → 6 MB).

One self-contained page served from the binary, with no external requests. It follows the
system's light or dark theme; the *Auto / Light / Dark* switch in the header overrides it
and is remembered per browser.

A run that lost over 99.5% of a large output gets a warning to check it. The optimized text
is kept next to the original (gzip, same retention), so runs recorded before that show only
the original. Viewing either here does not mark the source as failing.
